- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1-2% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model shows persistent bias toward higher prices; apply downward bias correction, especially in early horizon.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive within 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag effect (i.e., forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak).
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
